articles.title: Gakpo denies Klopp perfect start as Xavi’s Netherlands rescue draw against Germany
articles.summary: At least Germany can be sure it will not be dull. Jürgen Klopp had predicted his debut as head coach could be wild, a trait he would accept as long as his team were lively enough.
body: World domination is a far-off prospect for both of these flailing giants on such scrappy, frenetic evidence. But at least those with a stake in this famous old fixture, largely shorn of the spite and spit that defined it of old, could come away feeling something. Restoring those essential sensations of joy, pain and meaning sits at the very top of Klopp’s priorities. Germany looked raw and scattergun for long periods, reined in only by their lack of technical aptitude, but there were signs of an energy that had long been missing.

Nonetheless it was the more understated Xavi, making his own bow in charge of the hosts, who could punch the air in added time after Gakpo volleyed in a wonderful outside-of-the-boot cross from the substitute Ruben van Bommel. It so happens that the 22-year-old Van Bommel is son of the 79-times capped Mark; his grandfather is the former Netherlands manager Bert van Marwijk. An enthusiastic if largely toothless performance from Xavi’s crop was a reminder that the stardust of Van Bommel senior’s day is largely absent now; the equaliser’s conception, though, left lingering promise that the past can birth a brighter future.

The 20-year-old ran to the corner flag, grabbed it and made a gun-firing gesture during his celebration.

Austria regained ⁠the lead in the 90th minute through ​Phillipp ​Mwene, who scored via Paul ​Wanner’s cross. ‌Sasa Kalajdzic ​added ​a third in stoppage time with a close-range finish.

articles.summary: Republic of Ireland winger Chiedozie Ogbene urges the public to not "put the pressure on us" over the campaign to boycott the upcoming Nations League games against Israel.
body: The sides are due to meet in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday before the return fixture in Backa Topola, Serbia on 4 October (both 19:45 BST).

Since the sides were drawn together in Group B3, there has been increasing calls in Ireland to withdraw from the games due to the ongoing situation in Gaza with a 'Stop The Game' campaign gathering pace.

In the lead up to Thursday's 1-0 defeat by Kosovo in Pristina stand-in captain Dara O'Shea confirmed the players would meet on Friday to discuss their approach to Sunday's 'home' game for Israel, which will have no Irish fans in attendance before their behind-closed-doors match the following week.
"I'm aware of the feelings towards it," Ogbene told RTE Sport after Thursday's loss.

articles.title: ‘It’s not in us’: Anthony Gordon backs Tuchel over England’s possession problem
articles.summary: Barcelona winger says England cannot play like Spain. Gordon: ‘The Mexico game set us up a bit’ Anthony Gordon has sided with Thomas Tuchel’s assertion that controlling games through possession is not part of English football’s DNA.
body: England’s perennial struggle to keep the ball when under pressure flared when a place in the final was within touching distance in July, allowing Argentina to fight back and go through with two late goals. The pain has not gone away and there has been intense scrutiny of Tuchel’s role in Atlanta. The head coach’s tactical choices were criticised and he faced a backlash after saying “ball possession” was not in his team’s DNA.

But Gordon, who thinks he will always be scarred by losing against Argentina, sided with Tuchel’s observations about England’s style as he looked towards the Nations League game against Spain on Saturday. The 25-year-old admitted the side had an ingrained inability to control games but argued they should stop trying to copy other nations.
Gordon has gained an insight into the Spanish understanding of how to use the ball since his move to Barcelona. His view is that England should lean more into their physical strengths.

articles.title: João Félix strike for Portugal enough to sink Wales but Ronaldo fever falls flat
articles.summary: There was a comic-strip feel to another eventful evening in the kingdom of Cristiano Ronaldo. Where to start? It was the 67th minute when his No 7 went up on the fourth official’s board, the cue to remove the captain’s armband from his left bicep before departing to a universal ovation, but for the…
body: The referee, Donatas Rumsas, hurried him off the pitch but Ronaldo, his hair glazed copper, was presumably ruminating on a series of missed chances, a sitter from a few yards at the start of the second half, and his disallowed goal, after skating offside to latch on to a Bruno Fernandes pass. The grandiose “Siu” celebration went to waste, though try telling that to the locals who worship him.

In the end, Portugal began their defence of the Nations League with a narrow victory courtesy of another Al-Nassr forward, João Felix’s deflected first-half strike from the edge of the box beating Danny Ward in goal.

Many of the Wales squad have been lightly raced of late, but they could have snatched a late equaliser when Brennan Johnson hit the crossbar and Rúben Dias desperately denied Lewis Koumas, who again impressed Craig Bellamy. For Wales, this was an exhaustive physical effort and afterwards the head coach, citing his own experiences as a player, referenced how mentally sapping games against elite opposition can prove. “I needed an ice pack on my head,” Bellamy said.

articles.title: U.S. takes narrow lead over Internationals after Thursday fourballs at 2026 Presidents Cup
articles.summary: The U.S. may be looking for its 11th consecutive Presidents Cup victory, but the Internationals showed during Thursday's opening matches that they are ready to fight for their first victory since 1998.
body: The U.S. eked out a 3-2 session win over the International team as the 2026 Presidents Cup got underway with fourball matches at Medinah Golf Club on Thursday.

This is the closest the Cup has been after session one since the International team took a 4-1 lead after the opening day in 2019 (the U.S. would go on to win 16-14 with Tiger Woods as captain). The U.S. is looking for its 11th consecutive Presidents Cup win while the Internationals are looking for their second.

"A session win is a session win; we're going to take it any way we can get it," 2026 U.S. captain Brandt Snedeker said. "So happy for Scottie and Sam to go out there in that lead match and get that big win for us to lead us off. This is a long week. This is one session. We've got four more to go."

Scheffler and Burns won their first match together at either a Presidents Cup or Ryder Cup. Prior to Thursday, they were a combined 0-3-1 at the 2022 Presidents Cup and 2023 Ryder Cup. The best friends weren't paired together for the past two Cups before Snedeker gave them another shot.

articles.title: Sigh of Relief: NCAA Clears French Point Guard Nathan De Sousa
articles.summary: Finally, at least one true floor leader is guaranteed to suit up for coach Mark Few and the Gonzaga Bulldogs in the highly anticipated 2026-27 campaign. BeBasket was the first to report yesterday that Nathan De Sousa has been cleared to play this upcoming season.
body: De Sousa has been a member of France’s top league, LNB Elite, for the past five seasons with Cholet Basket, a club that also competes in the Basketball Champions League and Euro Cup.

In 2025-26, he averaged 10.9 points on a 44.7 field goal percentage/36.1 three-point percentage/76.9 free throw percentage, 4.9 assists, 2.5 rebounds, and 0.9 steals across 29 games with Cholet Basket in France’s LNB Elite.

De Sousa looks to follow in the footsteps of many legendary Frenchmen to be a part of the Pacific Northwest program’s legacy, like Ronny Turiaf, Killian Tillie, Joel Ayayi, and even Jean-Claude Lefebvre, the first native of France to be drafted in the NBA all the way back in 1960.

A lift off Gonzaga’s shoulders with their ongoing backcourt concerns throughout this chaotic offseason. While this positive announcement means it will just be one year for De Sousa repping the Zags, one has to think that Spain’s Real Madrid forward/center Izan Almansa will also receive a single season of eligibility to compete inside the McCarthey Athletic Center.

articles.title: Buttler injury halts England as Sri Lanka level series
articles.summary: Jos Buttler's bravery comes in vain as Sri Lanka fight back to beat England in the second one-day international at Headingley and set up a series decider at The Oval.
body: Needing 68 from 75 balls, England were cruising towards a target of 322 until Buttler retired hurt on 67 after tweaking a hamstring.
When Rehan Ahmed, Gus Atkinson and Jamie Overton fell, Buttler re-emerged with 27 needed from 14 balls and witnessed Will Jacks fall for 52 at the non-striker's end.
England were left needing 19 from the last with Buttler on strike but, barely able to hobble a single, he holed out at deep mid-wicket. England finished on 306-9 as Sri Lanka won by 16 runs.

Buttler had earlier shown flashes of his vintage best in hitting Sri Lanka's spinners for five sixes, putting England on course after collapse of 3-14 spoiled an opening stand of 143 between Tom Banton and Ben Duckett.

articles.summary: The US begin their bid to win an 11th consecutive Presidents Cup by opening up a 3-2 lead over the International team on day one.
body: The United States began their bid to win an 11th consecutive Presidents Cup by opening up a 3-2 lead over the International team at the end of Thursday's fourballs matches at Medinah Country Club in Illinois.
Justin Thomas and rookie Jackson Koivun put the first point on the board for Brandt Snedeker's American team with a resounding 4&3 win over Canada's Corey Conners and Colombia's Nico Echavarria.

World number one Scottie Scheffler, who was partnered with his long-time friend Sam Burns, took the 17th hole and held on to close out their victory over Min Woo Lee and Sungjae Im, who were left to rue several missed putts down the stretch.
And two-time major champions Wyndham Clark and Collin Morikawa ensured the US would take an advantage into Friday's five foursome matches.

articles.title: Alcaraz felt burnt out after too much exposure on and off the court
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz has admitted feeling burnt out due to being exposed to a lot of commitments before he suffered a lengthy layoff due to an injury sustained in April.
body: The Spaniard, who won the Australian Open title at the start of the year, was forced to miss more than four months from tennis because of a right wrist injury.
Alcaraz returned at the US Open where he reached the quarter-finals before losing a five-set thriller to American Ben Shelton, which finished at 3.33am local time.
Due to the demanding nature of the calendar, the former world No 1 has said he plans to take longer breaks from the game in the future and skip some tournaments.
"With the breaks I cannot plan them in advance," Alcaraz told Sky's Jacquie Beltrao at London's O2. "It depends how I feel mentally and physically.

articles.title: Late Gakpo strike denies Klopp winning start with Germany
articles.summary: Cody Gakpo hit a stoppage-time volley to earn the Netherlands a 1-1 draw against Germany in their Nations League Group A2 opener on Thursday, denying Jurgen Klopp victory in his first match as Germany boss.
body: Former Liverpool manager Klopp took charge in July after their surprise early exit from the World Cup against Paraguay in the last 32 under Julian Nagelsmann.
His side appeared set to give him the perfect start after Felix Nmecha put Germany ahead, but Gakpo finished off a swift counter-attack in the closing stages to level the contest.

The result also gave Xavi Hernandez something to celebrate in his first game in charge of the Netherlands. He was appointed in August after Ronald Koeman stepped down following the Dutch side's elimination at the same stage of the World Cup.

Germany suffered an early blow when Jamal Musiala was ruled out before kick-off, after experiencing muscle pain - and they were given a scare when Virgil van Dijk headed in from a corner inside the first 15 minutes.

articles.title: The Brewers Won 100 Games For The 1st Time (And These 5 Teams Still Never Have)
articles.summary: The Brewers extended their best-ever regular season with their first-ever 100th win. A number of MLB teams have still never reached triple digits, though.
body: The Brewers won their 100th game of the season on Thursday with a 5-1 victory over the Philadelphia Phillies, the first-ever time that Milwaukee has reached the 100-win mark. Before the 2026 season, the Brewers had not even won 99 games in a season before, nor 98 – Milwaukee reached those figures on Wednesday and Sunday, respectively, setting a new franchise record each time.

The elusive 100 has now been reached, though, after not all that many close calls. The 2025 Brewers won 97 games for the first time in franchise history, which dates back to 1969 when the Seattle Pilots were introduced to the league before shifting to Milwaukee for the 1970 season. Before ‘25, the Brewers’ best-ever regular season was 96 wins, achieved first in 2011 then again in 2018. The 1982 and 2021 squads won 95 each: the organization has just six other 90-plus-win seasons besides these.
